task_instance: Run a single-prompt LLM inference with llama.cpp on CPU: use the llama-cli binary to load a GGUF-quantized model (e.g. llama-2-7b-chat.Q4_K_M.gguf) and generate a short chat completion for the prompt 'Explain quantum computing' with a max-token limit, as shown in the skill's Quick start / Run inference section.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is actually running LLM inference, which requires installing/building the llama.cpp toolchain (brew install, git clone + make, or pip install of the Python binding) and then executing a compiled native binary (llama-cli / llama-server) against a multi-gigabyte downloaded GGUF model file. The office-assistant runtime grants only reading/writing/editing text files and web fetch/search; it cannot run any shell command, cannot install or build software, cannot execute code or native binaries, and cannot hold/execute large binary model files. There is no way to produce or verify the inference output (generated tokens) without executing code, so the core intent cannot be exercised in this runtime.
evidence: Read the SKILL.md at the skill path. Its Quick start, Server mode, Hardware acceleration and Common patterns sections consist entirely of shell commands: 'brew install llama.cpp' / 'git clone ... && make', 'huggingface-cli download ...' to fetch a .gguf binary model, and './llama-cli -m model.gguf -p ... -n 256' (plus './llama-server' and 'curl' against a running server) to generate output. Every one of these needs command execution, software installation, a native binary, and a large binary GGUF model file. None of these abilities exist in the read/write-text + web runtime, and no text-only deliverable substitutes for actually generating inference tokens. Per the run's rule against writing replacements/stubs for a missing bundled program, I did not fabricate a mock of llama-cli or its output. No work directory command was run (shell disallowed); result.json written directly to the work directory via the Write tool.
